overview: The bpf-next mailing list saw three notable patch series on August 29-30, 2026. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi posted a 6-patch series introducing a file descriptor interface for BPF program streams, enabling userspace to consume stream output via standard poll/read semantics. Yonghong Song sent v4 of a 12-patch series extending the BPF verifier and kfunc infrastructure to allow arena pointers to be returned by value from global functions and kfuncs.

patches.title: bpf: Add file descriptor interface for program streams
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This patch introduces the core kernel-side implementation of a file descriptor interface for BPF program streams. It allows userspace to open a stream associated with a running BPF program and interact with it using standard file operations. The motivation is to give tools like bpftool and custom user daemons a structured, pollable interface to consume BPF stream output without polling shared maps. The patch wires up the new stream FD into the BPF syscall layer and defines the read/poll/release file operations backed by the stream ring buffer.

patches.title: bpf: Defer stream file notifications from NMI context
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: BPF streams can be written from NMI context, but file system wake-up notifications (used to wake poll waiters) are not safe to call from NMI. This patch defers those wake-up calls to a safe context using an irq_work mechanism, ensuring stream consumers receive timely notifications without triggering NMI-unsafe code paths. It is a prerequisite for the broader stream FD series to function correctly across all BPF program types, including those attached to perf events.

patches.title: libbpf: Add bpf_prog_stream_open()
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This patch adds a new libbpf API, bpf_prog_stream_open(), that lets userspace open a file descriptor for a BPF program's output stream. The function wraps the new BPF syscall command introduced in the kernel-side patches and returns an fd suitable for use with read(), poll(), and epoll(). It integrates cleanly with the existing libbpf object model, taking a bpf_program pointer and returning a raw fd.

patches.title: bpf: allow terminal gotox instructions
patches.author: Siddharth Chintamaneni
patches.summary: The BPF verifier currently rejects programs where a gotox instruction appears as the last (terminal) instruction in a function, even when the jump target is valid. This patch relaxes that restriction to accommodate compiler-generated code patterns that legitimately use gotox at function exit. The change is confined to the verifier's instruction classification logic and does not affect the runtime semantics of gotox. A selftest in patch 2/2 exercises the newly allowed compiler-layout pattern.

patches.title: bpf: Allow a global function to return arena pointers by value
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: Previously, global BPF functions could not return structs containing arena pointers as by-value returns because the verifier lacked the type-checking infrastructure to validate them. This patch extends the verifier's by-value struct walk to recognize arena pointer members, allowing functions that allocate from a BPF arena to hand back the result in a struct. It enables more ergonomic arena-based memory management patterns without requiring callers to pass output pointers.

patches.title: bpf: Allow arena pointers in a by-value kfunc return
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: Complementing the global-function patch, this change extends support for arena pointers in by-value returns to kfuncs. Kfuncs that allocate arena memory and want to return it packed in a struct can now do so without triggering a verifier rejection. The implementation reuses the btf_type_is_arena_ptr() helper introduced earlier in the same series and hooks into the existing kfunc return-type validation path.
